bounding_design.shape: Two-regime deterministic function of (prefix, components, pane). VERBATIM: the existing lowercase bytewise UTF-8 hex, emitted whenever the FULL composed route INCLUDING its .pane- scope already fits 256 bytes. DIGESTED: zsha256-<64 hex> per component, only on overrun.
bounding_design.injectivity: STRUCTURAL, not asserted: the sentinel character z lies OUTSIDE the lowercase-hex alphabet and . never occurs inside a component, so a route parses back to its component tuple unambiguously and distinct tuples yield distinct routes. Under the digested regime this rests on SHA-256 collision resistance - cryptographic rather than absolute, and the code says so plainly rather than overclaiming.
bounding_design.resolvability_handled_honestly: Exact string reversal is MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE for a bounded encoding of unbounded input, and the agent did not fake it. hit_identity_from_result_author_id keeps its exact contract for the verbatim regime and honestly returns None for a digested one; a new TOTAL function hit_identity_from_result_author_id_in resolves any route by recomputation against the live candidate set - which is exactly how the production panel already matches an activated row.
bounding_design.byte_identity_is_structural: The verbatim branch is tried FIRST against the FINAL composed string, so byte-identity for anything that already fits is structural rather than incidental. mt113_every_route_that_fits_is_byte_identical_to_the_legacy_composition reproduces the real legacy algorithm inline and asserts equality over the adversarial corpus x 6 composition sites x 3 pane scopes. This is WHY a reserve-based budget was rejected: it would have changed MT-029 own 209-byte mounted route.
bounding_design.ordering_fix: Content-derived routes now compose their pane scope in the SAME call (pane_scoped_*_author_id), because pane_scoped_author_id can only shrink the PANE component and never the content.

scope.summary: Bound author_id composition so that user-supplied content can never push a completion token past its byte budget and silently disable Argus observability for that control.

measured_defect.mechanism: SearchBookmark::stable_id() hex-encodes the query, and bookmark_*_author_id then hex-encodes THAT result - a 4x expansion of the original user bytes. MAX_CLICK_COMPLETION_AUTHOR_BYTES is 256 (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/action.rs line 55), so the composed id overruns and serialize_* returns None. The node then carries no completion token, the action can never terminalize, and its receipt is permanently indeterminate.
measured_defect.first_failing_input: A search query of just 23 CHARACTERS. Measured example: "authentication middleware refactor" (34 chars) produces a 304-byte author_id whose token is silently dropped. This is trivially reachable by a real operator.
measured_defect.budget_raising_is_not_a_fix: Raising the budget only moves the ceiling: 256 B -> 22 chars, 512 B -> 86, 1024 B -> 213, 2048 B -> 469. Every tier remains reachable by a real query, path, or document title. Raising it also weakens bounded-token flood control and is a SHARED contract change inherited by every MT that emits a token.
measured_defect.field_budget_asymmetry: The SAME id is legal as `context` (512 B, used by same-target tokens) but illegal as `pending_target` (256 B, used by observer tokens). A synchronous control therefore proves fine while its asynchronous sibling cannot - which is exactly why bookmark RESTORE passed while bookmark REMOVE did not. That asymmetry is itself a latent trap for future MTs.
measured_defect.silent_failure: serialize_* simply returns None. The node carries no value, the action becomes unprovable, and NO diagnostic is emitted anywhere. That silence is what made this cost a full proof cycle to discover.

recommended_direction_from_the_mt029_age: PREFERRED: stop putting unbounded user content in a durable author_id at all. The root defect is that SearchBookmark::stable_id() derives identity from free text. Mint a bounded id (Uuid::now_v7(), which HBR-INT-008 already REQUIRES for new id mint sites) and keep the content-derived value as a separate dedup key. This bounds the row id by construction at roughly 102 bytes AND stays reversible.

Where a content-derived id is genuinely unavoidable, hash ONLY the variable component behind a stable prefix. NOTE the trade-off: this loses exact reversibility, which MT-029 actively relies on (hit_identity_from_result_author_id and accesskit_result_ids_are_utf8_injective_and_exactly_reversible), so it must be applied per-component rather than globally.

Make the failure LOUD regardless of which option is chosen: a debug_assert! plus a typed completion-unavailable marker so an over-budget id surfaces at authoring time instead of becoming a silently unprovable action months later.
acceptance_criteria: AC-113-1: an author_id composed from ARBITRARY user content (query, path, title) can no longer exceed its token budget. Proven with a property-style test over long, multibyte and adversarial inputs, including the measured 23-character regression case.

AC-113-2: exact reversibility relied on by MT-029 is preserved where it is required. accesskit_result_ids_are_utf8_injective_and_exactly_reversible and hit_identity_from_result_author_id must still pass unchanged; if a component becomes non-reversible, prove nothing depending on reversibility consumes it.

AC-113-3: an over-budget id can no longer fail SILENTLY. A typed completion-unavailable signal is emitted and is visible to the proof surface, and a debug_assert! fires in debug builds at authoring time.

AC-113-4: the pending_target (256 B) versus context (512 B) asymmetry is resolved or explicitly documented as intentional, so a synchronous control and its asynchronous sibling cannot diverge in provability for the same id.
AC-113-5: bookmark REMOVE - the control that concretely failed - produces a terminal non-indeterminate receipt with a realistic long query, proving the fix at the exact site that exposed the defect.
AC-113-6: if any new id mint site is introduced, it uses Uuid::now_v7() per HBR-INT-008, not v4.
